Subject: Evaluation governance & acceptance tests — aligning on close rules

Evelyn —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Praxis is keen to move from pilot to a decision window, but we want to make sure governance and acceptance are ironed out before we commit procurement time. Two asks from our side: (1) a concise set of go/no-go rules and escape hatches if quality drifts during the trial, and (2) a short list of smoke/acceptance tests we can run on our side to validate integration + accuracy.

High level constraints: our procurement team needs a predictable cutover window (we've got a vendor review week on Oct 22), and our security/compliance folks want explicit evidence for audit logging and data retention behavior.

Can you send the MAP snapshot that lists success criteria, exit gates, and the acceptance test artifacts? If possible, include the minimal pass/fail thresholds so we can scope our internal verification work.

Thanks —
Peter

Hi Peter —

Appreciate the clear asks and the timeline. Attached is a distilled MAP snapshot (Praxis_MAP_v3.xlsx) plus the smoke test checklist. Summary highlights below — please treat this as our proposed governance that we'd like you to review and sign off before Oct 22 so procurement can proceed.

High-level success criteria (must all be met for green):
- Mean inference latency (99th pct) within 350ms for 95% of clinical QA traffic during the trial window.
- End-to-end error rate < 0.5% (server errors, timeouts) over a 48-hour rolling window.
- Mean clinician-facing accuracy (precision@k where applicable) within agreed baseline ±3% compared to control dataset.
- No data exfiltration incidents; audit logs available for sampling within 24 hours of request.

Exit gates / escape hatches (ordered):
1) Safety/PLATFORM: Any P0 incident (data leak, production-crippling outage) — immediate pause and rollback to previous baseline.
2) Quality drift: If accuracy drops >5% vs baseline for 3 consecutive days, we trigger a joint investigation & remediation sprint.
3) Latency regression: sustained 99th pct latency >600ms for more than four hours — automatic routing to lower-latency variant or scaled capacity.

Acceptance tests (minimal set to run at kickoff and weekly):
- Integration sanity: 20 sample end-to-end requests (from Praxis staging) — must return within 1s and match format contract.
- Smoke accuracy: 250 labeled samples (provided in drive) — pass if overall score >= agreed baseline -3%.
- Audit/log sampling: request 10 recent traces and confirm event IDs, timestamps, and obfuscation rules per spec.

Timeline (proposed):
- Oct 20: Redwood sends final MAP and smoke-test suite (attached).
- Oct 22: Procurement review (Praxis) — goal for signoff on commercial terms.
- Oct 25–29: pilot stabilization window (Redwood monitors and runs nightly concordance jobs).
- Nov 1: Target decision meeting (go/no-go).

I attached the MAP and a short change log. We kept the pass/fail thresholds conservative but pragmatic; if Praxis needs tighter tolerances we can highlight which items will affect cost (e.g., 99th pct latency SLOs).

Next steps: please confirm that the acceptance tests are sufficient and indicate who will run the initial smoke run on Oct 23. I'll schedule a 30-min alignment meeting for Oct 20 if that works for you.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Peter / Evelyn — quick technical notes on the smoke tests and acceptance thresholds from the runtime side:

- Latency: our 99th percentile numbers depend heavily on request-size distribution. For the Praxis staging corpus, please flag any long-sequence flows (>1k tokens) — those will skew the percentile. We recommend measuring both token-length stratified 99th pct and global 99th pct.
- Accuracy tests: provide a stratified sample (clinical notes, structured inputs, edge cases). We'll provide a scorer (python script) in the drive so you can reproduce locally. Pass threshold definition: overall >= baseline -3% AND no critical subgroup falling below baseline -7%.
- Audit logs: we'll deliver a sampling API that returns compact trace stubs (event id, model version, timestamp, obfuscation marker). Praxis should run the log sampling test and confirm fields.

Small ask: can Praxis share expected peak concurrent sessions for the test window (an estimate is fine)? That will help sizing capacity and avoiding latency spikes.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
